html:
Performers
Philharmonic-⁠Symphony Orchestra of New York (orchestra), Charles Munch (conductor), Édouard Nies-⁠Berger (organ), Walter Hendl (piano, four hands (listed in James North’s discography; uncredited on the labels)) Documented

The transferor says Nies-⁠Berger is credited on all labels but plays only on sides 3, 4, 7 and 8, and that the piano players are uncredited; MusicWeb’s review of the Pristine reissue names Walter Hendl and Arthur Schuller as pianists.

[1] [3]
Work version
First half of the symphony’s two large movements, as divided on the transferred 78 rpm set Documented

The transferor describes the contents of sides 1–⁠4. The labels do not give the tempo changes within each part.

[1]
Recorded
1947-11-10 Documented

Recorded on Monday 10 November 1947 per the transferor’s description; MusicWeb gives only “November 1947”.

[1]
Place
Carnegie Hall, New York City Documented[1] [3]
Label
Columbia Masterworks Documented

Issued in the United States in June 1948; also issued in France, Italy, the Netherlands and Britain.

[1]
Catalogue
MM-747 (12841-D to 12844-D); LP reissue ML-4120 Documented

Catalogue numbers as given by the transferor; no label has been inspected.

[1]
Matrix, take, sides
1–⁠4; matrices XCO 39319 to XCO 39326 Documented

The transferor prints the last matrix as XCO 38326, evidently a typing slip. Takes are not identified.

[1]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The Internet Archive item was uploaded on 31 March 2022 by a private collector; no transfer engineer is named.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Archive’s upload date is not a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

The Archive supplies FLAC and a VBR MP3 derivative; equalisation and speed correction are not described.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain: Saint-⁠Saëns died on 16 December 1921 Documented

More than seventy years after the composer’s death.

[5]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1948, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The programme’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applies: the transferor documents the June 1948 issue as Columbia MM-747, Pristine and MusicWeb confirm the November 1947 session as Munch’s first American recording, and Columbia’s printed record catalogue for 1949 lists the eight-side set MM-747 (Munch, Nies-⁠Berger). The 1948 catalog does not list it, which fits a mid-1948 issue. This is not US or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

Camille Saint-⁠Saëns, Symphony No. 3, Op. 78, Part I; Philharmonic-⁠Symphony Orchestra of New York, Charles Munch, Édouard Nies-⁠Berger (organ). Columbia Masterworks MM-747 (1948), Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only.
